updates.statement: Accuracy per step is set by the structure of the update, and on this base the update geometry looks saturated. Only two levers moved the 3-seed mean by >=0.5 pp: Muon on the conv filters (+1.3 pp, E014) and lookahead (~0.9-1 pp, E008/E020). Every structural update change since then has lost: Muon-C (E030 -1.2), weaker whitening at matched norm (E065 -1.51), NorMuon (E066 -0.26), a Muon head (E059 -0.61), batch-size schedules (E053 -0.49, E055 -0.45) and BN-bias lr x128 (E056 -0.49). Scalar re-tunes moved the mean by <=0.18 pp. The <=4.7 s target was reached by a freeze (E058), not by an update change. Three directions are left. (a) Check whether the lookahead edits ever took effect (H1.6.6). (b) Class-structured soft targets (Online Label Smoothing). (c) Stronger or more accurate whitening, which has a low prior because exact polar factors only match 4-5-step NS on LMs.
updates.reason: All four 'update-side levers left' that H1 named were refuted (E059, E066, E065, E053/E055), and its time target was met by E058's freeze. Rewritten around what is left, and confidence lowered.

updates.statement: Muon on the 4D conv filters cuts the epochs needed on CIFAR-100 by ~2.5 (9 SGD epochs -> ~6.5 Muon epochs). The working form is flattened [out, in*k*k] orthogonalized Nesterov momentum with NS3 at Frobenius scale 1 and a weight-norm projection. Nesterov SGD runs the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head, and lookahead is kept. Muon lr is flat from 0.16 to 0.24 (and 0.20 at bs 1536), 0.36 costs ~1 pp, and momentum 0.6-0.8 is flat. The filter geometry looks saturated in every direction tested: frequency-split (E030 -1.2), weaker whitening (E065 -1.51) and per-row normalization (E066 -0.26) all lost. Batch size is closed at 1536 (E055 -0.45 at 2048). Caveat: some 'flat' readings may be compile no-ops (H1.6.6).
updates.reason: Adds E065, E066 and E055 to the mechanism. Status unchanged: E014/E016-E022 support it strongly.

updates.statement: Muon lr below the tested range. On the current tip, lowering the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.11 with nothing else changed moves mean accuracy by no more than +-0.2 pp. If it holds, the lr axis is flat over 0.11-0.24, and the 0.36 cliff (E019) is a high-lr instability rather than an optimum near 0.16.
updates.reason: H1.9 is closed, so this no longer serves as a control for H1.9.1. It keeps value only as a map of the lr axis, so its priority drops.

External support: an ICLR 2026 batch-schedule paper (arxiv 2602.14208, LM only) finds late switches beat constant and early switches, which matches E053 (early switch -0.49). Still untested in vision with lookahead, and E055 (flat bs 2048, -0.45) caps the upside. With the 0.07 pp margin, it needs an accuracy gain to stack on.
E066: NorMuon cost -0.26 pp at the same time, past the pre-registered refute line. Together with E065 and E030, it points to saturated filter geometry.

updates.statement: With lookahead heavily weighting late iterates, the end of training matters through what it feeds the average. A non-zero tail lr supplies diverse iterates: decay-to-0 hurt (E025 -0.51 pp), a 0.15x floor was not better (E033 -0.17), and BN recalibration adds nothing (E035). The averaging setup itself (decay, sync interval, EMA on top) is effectively untested: E028's 0.97^5 change matched its parent to 0.003 pp, closer than E057's pure RNG shift (~0.1 pp per seed), so it was probably a compile no-op (H1.6.6).
updates.reason: E057 shows that real trajectory changes move per-seed results by ~0.1 pp, so E028's 0.003 pp match is implausible for a real change. The averaging axis should be treated as untested, not flat.

updates.statement: Some schedule or hyperparameter edits did not take effect in the compiled timed path, and the tip may still run lookahead 0.95^5. Check in drafts/: (1) log the per-sync alpha actually applied in the E058 compiled path; (2) compare the seed-0 final-weight hashes or norms of E027 vs E028, E045 vs E046 (Muon lr 0.20) and E047 vs E049 (head lr x3). Supported if any pair has identical weights or the logged alphas ignore the edit. In that case reopen the affected axes, H1.6.1 first.
updates.reason: Review: never executed, and E057's re-draw size makes E028's 0.003 pp match look like a no-op. It is a cheap check that decides whether the averaging axis (worth ~1 pp) was ever tested.

updates.statement: The SGD group (head, BN biases) is sensitive in the downward-lr and upward-BN directions. Head lr x0.5 cost 0.41 pp (E039), x2 and x3 are within noise (E045 +0.18, E049 -0.03), and BN-bias lr x128 cost 0.49 pp (E056). The head lr axis is closed above x1, and an orthogonalized head update hurt (E059). Only BN-bias lr x32 is untested.
updates.reason: E056 and E059 added. No positive lever was found in this group, and the one remaining probe (x32) is cheap.
Both one-factor changes tested with a clear signal lost (E039 -0.41, E056 -0.49), and head x2/x3 did not reach +0.25. The remaining candidate, BN x32, moves to a new node.
Jitter was +0.16 (E042, inconclusive), and dropping translate in the low-res stages was neutral (E052 +0.04). Augmentation strength is not a visible lever at this horizon.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip at its epoch count, removing translate-2 in ALL stages (including 32 px), while keeping the alternating flip, gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at equal or lower time. Untested: E052 removed translate only in the 20/28 px stages, which is a different test (see the new low-res-translate node).
updates.reason: Review: E052 was misattributed to this node. It tested translate off in the low-res stages only. The node stays untested.
E052 found low-res augmentation (translate) neutral, which weakens the EfficientNetV2-style coupling argument (D018 also notes translate is not stronger at low res).

updates.statement: How strongly Muon orthogonalizes should be scheduled over training, with weaker, less whitened updates late (Hiverge's Frobenius-scale schedule 0.50->0.08 before NS3). Refuted by E065: -1.51 pp with the update RMS meant to be matched. Caveat: the drafts/ log of per-group update norms was not reported. If the norms did not match, E065 also changed the effective Muon lr, and the 'test stronger, never weaker' lesson rests on one confounded run. Either way, this schedule hurts on this base.
updates.reason: E065 -1.51 pp, far beyond noise. Refuted regardless of attribution, but the norm-match caveat is kept as the review asked.
Parent refuted by E065. This unmatched-norm variant mixes the same weaker whitening with a lower effective lr and is not worth a run.
E059: Muon on the head cost -0.61 pp. The decay confound is noted, but a class-frequency-weighted SGD head update looks useful here (consistent with E066).
E059 -0.61 pp, past the -0.3 pp refute line.

updates.statement: With the recipe held fixed, per-step GPU work can still be cut by a few percent at unchanged accuracy, but only by removing GPU work: launch overhead is hidden (E005, E038), and whole-run CUDA graphs gave Fable only ~5 ms. Systems total so far is ~11% (E007, E010, E021, E023, E034), plus the curriculum FLOP cuts (H2.3) and the late block-1 freeze (E058 -4.7%). Candidates left: Gram Newton-Schulz (math-preserving, ~45-50% fewer NS FLOPs at aspect ratio 9), a trial-0 warmup-gap check on the many-variant tip (H3.2), re-checking max-autotune for the PCIe judge (H2.5.1), and Muon projection frequency (H2.4.3). Fewer NS iterations are now an accuracy risk (E065).
updates.reason: Updated with E058, Gram NS (search) and the E065 risk for NS2. Confidence lowered slightly because the remaining levers are each ~1%.

updates.statement: A resolution curriculum of bilinearly downsampled whole images (antialiased, inside the compiled augment) cuts FLOPs at small accuracy cost while the low-res steps fall in or near warmup. Current form: 20 px for epochs 0-1.5, 28 px for 1.5-3.5, then 32 px for 3.25 epochs. Prices: 24 px warmup -3.0%/+0.08 pp (E040); 24->20 px -3.5%/-0.18 (E047); 28 px stage -5.2%/+0.02 (E048, -0.23 in E044); 28 px to 3.5 epochs -1.5%/-0.10 (E051); 28 px to 4.0 epochs -2.3%/-0.22 (E054, infeasible). Low-res steps in the peak-lr phase cost more (E043 -0.38). 16 px collapses (E050 -1.41, 1x1 final map). The 32 px tail looks near its floor at ~3.25 epochs.
updates.reason: E051 and E054 added. The accuracy numerators are noise-sized, so the per-1% rates are uncertain by about +-0.1 pp.

updates.statement: Non-conv or redundant work that takes a visible share of GPU time can be cut at no accuracy cost by doing less of it. Instances: the atomic pool backward (E010 -2.0%), SiLU (E021 -2.2%), a batched compiled Muon step (E023 -2.7%), freezing the whitening bias after epoch 1 (E034 -3.0%), and freezing block 1 for the last 20% (E058 -4.7%). The remaining Muon cost (~1.4 ms/step) is GPU kernel time (E038). The best remaining cut is math-preserving Gram NS. Fewer NS iterations risk E065-style under-whitening.
updates.reason: E058 added as an instance, Gram NS added from search, and the NS2 risk noted from E065.
airbench94_muon projects every step, and the thinned schedule is a later speed tweak from Hiverge/Fable with no known accuracy gain. Expected saving is ~1%.

updates.statement: Cutting NS from 3 to 2 iterations with Turbo-Muon AOL preconditioning saves >=0.25 ms/step and >=1.2% mean time, with accuracy within +-0.15 pp. Gate in drafts/: on the tip's real momentum matrices, launch only if the fraction of singular values >0.5 after NS2+AOL is at least NS3's. Otherwise retire.
updates.reason: Search: Turbo-Muon's own airbench result was -0.8% end-to-end, below this node's 1.2% target. E065 shows that weaker whitening falls off a cliff, so NS2 is an accuracy risk. Gated.

updates.statement: Two NS iterations with Polar Express coefficients recomputed via optimal_composition(num_iters=2, l = measured smallest singular-value ratio of the tip's momentum matrices) save >=0.2 ms/step and >=1% mean time, with accuracy within +-0.2 pp. Do not truncate the published 5-step list. Gate in drafts/: launch only if the post-NS spectrum (fraction >0.5) matches or exceeds NS3's.
updates.reason: Search supplied the exact coefficient recipe. E065 makes matched whitening strength a hard gate. Gram NS (same math) is the safer first Muon-cost cut.

updates.statement: FreezeOut-style: freezing block 1 (conv weights and BN biases) for the last ~20% of samples, through a compiled variant that detaches block 1's output plus a Muon variant without its group, cuts mean time by >=3% with accuracy within -0.2 pp (E058: -4.7%, -0.09 pp). Earlier (0.7: E061 -0.11 pp, infeasible by 0.04), block-2 cascade (E062 -0.49) and mid-run thinning (E064 -0.54) are worse. The 0.7 point is unresolved, not closed.
updates.reason: E058 met the prediction, so the node is supported, not 'open 0.10'. Confidence is held at 0.6 because the accuracy delta is noise-sized and the margin is 0.07 pp. Mechanism moved to the new per-block Lvl1.

Search: the A100 PCIe has a 300 W cap vs 400 W SXM and ~5% less bandwidth, so kernel choices autotuned on SXM may not transfer. Build time (228+ s, more variants with each change) is also approaching the 600 s limit.

updates.statement: After clearing the Inductor cache, run the E058 tip and an E058 variant without cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune 2-3 times each, interleaved. The paired mean time gap will be <1.5%, meaning the E007 keep was within jitter. In that case drop max-autotune to free build budget and remove SXM-specific tuning.
updates.reason: Retargeted to the current tip, per the review.
No evidence tokens, and not re-verified on the many-variant tip (E058's per-trial times are unreported). Confidence lowered until the trial-0 check (new node) is done.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy gate, and the 3-seed mean is optimistically biased for the 40-seed judge. The tip (E058, 0.7537) clears 0.753 by 0.07 pp. It was reached by keeping noise-sized changes (E051 -0.10, E052 +0.04, E058 -0.09) and discarding equally close misses (E044, E054, E061: 0.03-0.06 pp below the gate). That ratchet selects on seeds 0-2. Two noise estimates conflict: E057's single RNG shift implies ~0.06 pp sd on the mean, while E044 vs E048 (the same 28 px stage, -0.23 vs +0.02) implies ~0.12-0.15. Until extra seeds are run, deltas below ~0.25 pp are inconclusive, and the tip's true mean is likely at or below 0.753.
updates.reason: Review: the margin is now 0.07 pp, built by a ratchet, and the extra-seed checks were never run. Confidence raised that this is the binding issue.

updates.statement: A bit-identical commit reruns deterministically in accuracy, with ~1% timing jitter (E003). The paired re-draw sd for a real recipe change is unresolved. E057 (one RNG shift on the Muon+curriculum base) gave per-seed deltas of -0.07/+0.12/+0.09, implying ~0.06 pp on the 3-seed mean, but that is a single draw. E044 vs E048 suggests ~0.12-0.15 pp. airbench reports a per-run sd of 0.116-0.157 pp on CIFAR-10 (10,000 runs), a lower bound for CIFAR-100 near its knee.
updates.reason: The two noise models are now stated together, and the search lower bound is added. It cannot be resolved without more draws.

updates.statement: Offline in drafts/, evaluating the E058 tip on extra seeds 3-12 gives a per-seed sd of 0.12-0.3 pp and an extra-seed mean within 0.05 pp of, or above, the seeds 0-2 mean (0.7537). This would mean the ratchet did not inflate the tip. Refuted if the extra-seed mean is <=0.7525; in that case, recover margin before cutting more time.
updates.reason: Retargeted to E058, with the threshold tightened to the 0.07 pp margin. Prior lowered because selection on fixed seeds favours a downward shift. This is the top-priority check.
Superseded: whether E024/E026 were re-draws matters only for the tip's margin, which H4.1.2 measures directly on E058.
Only one of the four pre-registered edits was run (E057, the RNG shift). One draw cannot estimate an sd, and it conflicts with E044/E048. More draws are needed (new noise node).

updates.statement: Time is set by full-resolution compute after warmup. Warmup steps tolerate low resolution (E040, E047, E048) but not fewer steps: the early phase is step-starved (E053, bs 2048 there -0.49 pp). Low-res steps after the lr peak cost accuracy (E043 -0.38; E054 -0.22 for the 3.5->4.0 boundary), so the 32 px tail is near its floor at ~3.25 epochs, and the final map must stay >=2x2 (E050). The remaining levers on this axis are the total epoch count on the curriculum+freeze base (E063 suggests the marginal 32 px epoch is now worth only ~0.3 pp) and per-block freezing (new Lvl1).
updates.reason: Review: H6 did not explain E053 (step-starved early phase) or E058 (per-block cuts). Rewritten, and confidence lowered. Per-layer timing moves to a new Lvl1.

updates.statement: The 16 px collapse (E050, -1.41 pp) comes from a structural threshold: at 16 px the final map is 1x1, so global max-pool selection vanishes. The other candidate, the whitening bias being fitted at low res and then frozen, is now unlikely: training it through 3.5 epochs gave no gain (E060 -0.14).
updates.reason: E060 removed most of the whitening-bias half of the mechanism. The 1x1-map story is untested.
E060: training the whitening bias to 3.5 epochs gave -0.14 pp, not >=+0.2. Whitening-bias axis closed (with E034).

updates.statement: Diagnostic. On the tip, replacing the 20 px first stage with 18 px keeps a 2x2 final map (whitening 17 -> pools 8/4/2), and mean accuracy stays within -0.25 pp of the tip. A loss of >=0.6 pp would mean the 1x1-map story does not explain E050. Time saving is expected to be <1% (E050: 20->16 px saved only 0.8%, since small maps are latency-bound), so this is mainly a mechanism test.
updates.reason: E050 showed that small-map stages save little time, so the >=1% time prediction was unrealistic. Reframed as a diagnostic, with lower priority given the margin.
E053: bs 2048 in the low-res stages cost 0.49 pp for -2.1%. The early phase is step-starved, not latency-tolerant. This matches the late-switch literature (arxiv 2602.14208).
The milder setting (bs 2048, E053) already lost 0.49 pp, so bs 3072 in the low-res stages would be worse.
28 px extended to 3.5 epochs cost -0.10 (E051, kept) and to 4.0 cost -0.22 (E054, infeasible). The cost per half-epoch is rising, but each step is noise-sized.
Run in two halves: E051 (-0.10 pp, -1.5%) and E054 (-0.22 pp, -2.3%, infeasible by 0.06). Combined, ~-0.32 pp for ~-3.8%. Neither side of the prediction is cleanly met.

new.statement: Each block's late learning value runs out at a different time, so compute can be removed per block once its value is spent, but step count must be kept early. Block 1 is nearly done by ~0.7-0.8 of training (E058 -0.09 pp for -4.7%; E061 -0.11 for -2.8%). Block 2 is still learning at 0.9 (E062 -0.49 for 4.4%). Thinning block 1's mid-run updates hurts (E064 -0.54). Early steps cannot be removed at all (E053). The levers left are refinements of the block-1 freeze (how it is entered, what the frozen block still computes) and partial freezes inside block 2.

Part of the cost of an earlier block-1 freeze comes from stopping abruptly while the Muon lr is still well above its floor: the last fast iterates of block 1 are noisy, and lookahead pulls the slow weights onto them. Annealing block 1's own lr to zero before the freeze (FreezeOut's per-layer cosine-to-zero) lets the freeze point move earlier at no extra accuracy cost. This is not the global decay-to-0 that hurt in E025.

On E058, linearly anneal block 1's Muon lr multiplier and its BN-bias lr from the global schedule value to 0 over samples 0.6-0.7 of training, then switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair at 0.7 (E061's point). All other groups keep their schedules. Prediction: mean time matches E061 (about -2.8% vs E058), and accuracy is within -0.05 pp of E058, better than E061's -0.11. Run only after the extra-seed margin check (H4.1.2).

After block 1 is frozen, its forward still computes train-mode BN batch statistics and running-stat updates that no later step needs. Running the frozen block as a pure inference block (eval-mode BN, or BN folded into the conv) removes that work. Block 2 may rely on the batch-stat noise, though, which would cost accuracy.

On E058, from the 0.8 freeze onward, run block 1 in eval mode (its running stats as of the freeze, no further updates) inside the frozen graph variant. Prediction: mean time falls by >=0.7% with accuracy within +-0.15 pp. A loss of >=0.25 pp means block 2 depends on block 1's batch-stat noise.

Late learning inside block 2 is uneven. Its first conv, which reads a frozen block 1, has less left to learn than its later convs and BN affine, so it can be frozen alone without cutting gradient to anything upstream that still trains.

On E058, for the last 10% of samples, also freeze only block 2's first conv: no wgrad, removed from its Muon shape group, with block 2's later convs and BN biases still training. Prediction: mean time falls by >=1% with accuracy within -0.1 pp of E058. A loss of >=0.25 pp, like E062's, would mean all of block 2 is still learning late.

On the curriculum+freeze base, the marginal 32 px epoch is worth far less than the ~1.14 pp/epoch measured at 6.5-7 epochs on the plain Muon base: E063 bought +0.07 pp for +0.25 epoch. If that holds, the plain total epoch count is the cheapest time lever left. The alternative readings are that E063 was a noisy single comparison, or that its moved freeze points and lookahead ramp confounded it.

E058 at 6.5 total epochs: 0.25 epoch removed from the 32 px stage, stage boundaries kept in samples, block-1 freeze kept at 0.8 of total samples, and every schedule scaled to samples seen. Prediction: mean time falls by >=3% and accuracy by <=0.1 pp. A drop of >=0.25 pp restores the steep-slope picture, and E063 was noise. Run only after the extra-seed margin check, because the gate margin is 0.07 pp.

Uniform label smoothing is flat from 0.1 to 0.3 (E004, E036), but class-structured soft targets are a different, untested change. CIFAR-100's superclasses give a strong similarity structure. Online Label Smoothing builds per-class soft targets from the model's own correct predictions, giving a richer gradient per step at negligible compute (a 100x100 scatter-add).

On the tip, replace LS 0.2 with Online Label Smoothing. A 100x100 GPU matrix S, reset in prepare(), accumulates the softmax of correctly classified training samples into their class column inside the compiled step. S is column-normalized and swapped in every half-epoch, uniform/LS for the first half-epoch. Loss = 0.5*CE(hard) + 0.5*CE(soft from S). Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Likely failure mode: the 300-epoch gain (+1.1 pp over LS on ResNet-56) needs a stable S, which 6.75 epochs may not give.

Stronger whitening than NS3 (NS4 with the same coefficients, or 3 iterations with Polar Express coefficients recomputed via optimal_composition(num_iters=3)) at the same update norm gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy on the tip at <=1% more time. Low prior: on GPT-2, exact SVD polar factors were no better than 4-5-step NS, and E017 showed NS5 ~= NS3. This is the only update-geometry direction E065 leaves open.

Replacing the tip's batched NS3 with Gram Newton-Schulz (iterate on the out x out Gram matrix, using 2 rectangular GEMMs instead of 2 per iteration, same quintic coefficients, fp16) gives the same Muon update up to rounding. Every flattened filter has aspect ratio 9, so this should cut NS FLOPs by ~45%. Prediction: Muon GPU time falls by >=0.3 ms/step (drafts/time_muon.py), mean time by >=1%, and accuracy stays within +-0.15 pp. Gate: check the max deviation from the NS3 output on real momentum matrices and run debug_nan for fp16 overflow under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.

Offline in drafts/ on the E058 tip, 3 further RNG-shift edits (1, 2 and 3 extra dummy draws from the trial generator) give a paired per-seed sd of <=0.1 pp, i.e. <=0.06 pp on the 3-seed mean, confirming E057. If the sd is >=0.15 pp per seed, the E057 estimate was low, and every keep or close since E057 that rested on a |delta| < 0.25 pp is inconclusive.

On the E058 tip, with its many compiled variants (20/28/32 px, with and without whitening-bias grad, block-1 frozen and unfrozen, partial shapes at 4+ switches), trial 0's train time exceeds the mean of trials 1-2 by >1%. That would be a warmup gap like E035's. Finding and warming the missing shape or layout then cuts mean time by >=0.5% at identical accuracy. Refuted if the trial-0 excess is <=0.5%.

Turning off translate-2 in the 20/28 px stages, while keeping it at 32 px, is accuracy-neutral (within +-0.15 pp; E052 +0.04 pp). Augmentation in the low-res stages is not what limits them, so EfficientNetV2-style coupling of augmentation to resolution is not a lever at this horizon.

On the tip, lowering the BN-bias lr multiplier from x64 to x32 (lr*wd held constant) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Low prior: x128 cost 0.49 pp (E056), which suggests x64 is at or slightly above the optimum, and the airbench x64 was tuned on CIFAR-10.

structured_output.summary:
I updated 49 nodes and added 18, mostly to roll in E051-E066 and the review's points.

**Margin (H4).** The tip, E058 at 0.7537, clears the 0.753 gate by only 0.07 pp. It got there by keeping noise-sized changes (E051, E052, E058) while discarding near-misses that were just as close (E044, E054, E061).
- H4 confidence is raised to 0.75.
- H4.1.2 now asks for E058 to be evaluated offline on seeds 3-12 and is the top priority.
- H4.1 now states two noise estimates that disagree: about 0.06 pp on the 3-seed mean (from E057) and about 0.12-0.15 pp (from E044 vs E048). H4.1.4 becomes inconclusive, and a new node asks for more random-seed-shift draws to settle it.

**Update geometry (H1).** H1 is rewritten and lowered to 0.30. Every "lever left" it named lost accuracy:
- Refuted: NorMuon (E066), Muon on the head (H1.10/H1.10.1), H1.7.1 and H6.1.1.
- H1.9 (scheduled whitening strength) is refuted by E065 (-1.51 pp). The caveat stays that E065's update-norm match was never reported. H1.9.1 is retired.
- H1.6.6 rises to 0.6: E028 matched its parent to 0.003 pp, so its lookahead change was probably never applied, and the averaging axis counts as untested.
- New nodes: stronger whitening (NS4 or Polar Express at 3 iterations), Online Label Smoothing as a class-structured target, and BN-bias lr x32.

**Systems (H2).**
- H2.4.7, freezing block 1 late (E058), is now supported at 0.6.
- NS2 variants (H2.4.5, H2.4.6) are demoted and gated on a check that they whiten as strongly as NS3, because of E065. Turbo-Muon also saved only 0.8% on its own benchmark.
- New: Gram Newton-Schulz, which keeps the same math and should cut Newton-Schulz FLOPs by about 45%, since every filter matrix has aspect ratio 9.
- New: a check for warmup gaps that slow trial 0.
- H2.5.1 is retargeted to the E058 tip, for the PCIe judging GPU and the build-time budget.

**Resolution and steps (H6).** H6 is rewritten and lowered to 0.5:
- The early phase cannot lose steps: H6.2 and H6.2.1 are refuted by E053.
- The 32 px tail is close to its floor: H6.3 and H6.3.1 are inconclusive.
- New N_TAIL: E063 suggests an extra 32 px epoch is worth little on the current base, so it tests E058 cut to 6.5 epochs.

**Per-block freezing (new Lvl1, N_FREEZE).** This covers why block 1 can be frozen cheaply late and block 2 cannot. It predicts three things:
- annealing block 1's lr before an earlier freeze point;
- running the frozen block 1 in eval mode;
- freezing only block 2's first conv late.

**Bookkeeping.** E052 was attached to the wrong node (H1.8.2). Its finding, that dropping translate in the low-res stages is neutral, now has its own node, N_AUG.

**Suggested order:** the extra-seed check, the compile no-op check, the trial-0 timing check, Gram NS, then E058 at 6.5 epochs.
